redistribution: Official NSTG text is not included. Cite FMoH, not this file, for clinical content.

provenance.cite: Federal Ministry of Health, Nigeria. Nigeria Standard Treatment Guidelines. 3rd edition. Abuja: Federal Ministry of Health; 2022.
provenance.note: Government communications sometimes use the abbreviation NTSG. Obtain the official book from FMoH or an authorised source.
provenance.this_file: Original short summaries for a research retriever. If a line conflicts with NSTG 2022, NSTG wins.

entries.name: Malaria (research index)
themes: Endemic Plasmodium transmission shapes fever work-up and differential diagnosis.
Uncomplicated versus severe disease is a clinical fork this index does not encode as a protocol.
Parasite clearance and supportive care are distinct computational concerns from oncology burden.
cautions: Fever and cytopenias can confound interpretation of treatment toxicity in a model that only sees X.
G6PD and pregnancy are classical pharmacologic cautions in antimalarial classes; this index does not list products.
Do not treat model 'infection_risk' as a malaria diagnosis.

entries.name: HIV (research index)
themes: Lifelong antiretroviral therapy continuity is a clinical priority this software does not schedule.
Immune competence in the ODE is not a CD4 count and must not be mapped one-to-one.
Opportunistic infection risk is a qualitative comorbidity theme for constraint tightening.
cautions: Immune-depleting computational effectors should be down-weighted; they are still not ART advice.
Drug–drug interaction tables live in official sources, not in this repository.
Do not interpret a rise in I as virologic control.

entries.name: Sickle cell disease (research index)
themes: Vaso-occlusive stress and chronic haemolytic anaemia are host-constraint themes.
Infection risk (including encapsulated organisms) is a recurring clinical motif.
Disease-modifying and crisis-care pathways belong in NSTG / specialist protocols, not this ODE.
cautions: Host-stress proxy X is a poor stand-in for acute chest, stroke, or sequestration — do not map it.
Tighter computational toxicity caps are a modelling choice, not a transfusion threshold.
Dehydration and hypoxia are clinical, not state variables here.

entries.name: Anaemia (research index)
themes: Anaemia is a syndrome: iron, haemolysis, chronic disease, malaria-related, and sickle-related paths differ.
Oxygen-carrying capacity is not modelled; X is not haemoglobin.
Supportive-care themes in oncology often intersect anaemia without implying a single cause.
cautions: Do not use peak X as a transfusion trigger.
Haemolysis-adjacent computational toxicity should be treated as a flag, not a Coombs result.
Classify cause in clinic; this index only tightens a cap.

entries.name: Oncology supportive care (research index)
themes: Suspected malignancy needs specialist referral; this software does not triage.
Supportive themes include infection, anaemia, pain, and organ-stress monitoring.
Systemic anticancer therapy and biologics are product-specific; we only carry class-level caricatures.
cautions: Febrile neutropenia is a clinical emergency pathway, not an ODE event.
Tumour-lysis and infusion reactions are unmodelled.
Pain ladders and antiemetic tables are NSTG/clinical content — omitted here.

entries.name: Febrile neutropenia theme (research index)
themes: Fever plus neutropenia is a time-critical clinical motif in anticancer therapy.
The ODE has no neutrophil count; infection_risk_weight is a scalar, not a culture.
cautions: Never delay real-world work-up because a simulation looks 'stable'.
This entry only increases infection-risk weighting in search.

entries.name: Palliative / cancer pain theme (research index)
themes: Pain assessment and stepwise analgesia are clinical guideline topics.
Burden B is not a pain score.
cautions: This pipeline does not recommend analgesics or palliative regimens.
Do not treat a falling B as symptom control.

entries.name: Pregnancy theme (research index)
themes: Pregnancy changes risk–benefit for almost every systemic class.
This index records the theme; it does not encode obstetric protocols.
cautions: Do not run this tool as a pregnancy-safety checker.
Teratology and antimalarial/ART choices belong in official sources.

entries.name: Tuberculosis theme (research index)
themes: TB–HIV overlap is a major Nigerian clinical context.
Immune restoration and infection unmasking are not states in MHBD-4.
cautions: Checkpoint-like immune stimulation in silico is not IRIS prediction.
Rifamycin interaction tables are omitted on purpose.
